description: Source-derived synthetic scenarios with agent-authored reference labels. Text is paraphrased, not a copy of the linked article. Inventory is fictional. Complete means the supplied scenario is complete, not that the original page was reproduced. This small set is not a production accuracy benchmark.

node-dns.title: Node.js DNS security disclosure
node-dns.description: The October 21 advisory describes CVE-2026-105482: Node.js DNS methods can truncate hostnames at a NUL byte. Applications that validate a hostname and then call dns.resolve or dns.reverse can resolve a different name. Affected release lines are Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x. Security releases 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 contain fixes. The advisory concerns the Node.js runtime, not every project hosted by its organization.

php-rce.title: PHP request-handling vulnerabilities disclosed
php-rce.description: PHP's October 21 advisory identifies CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which can permit remote code execution without authentication in web-serving PHP installations. Fixed releases are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PHP-FPM is among the affected deployments. Disabling session upload progress blocks confirmed paths for CVE-2026-109619 but is not a complete fix; updating is still required. Distribution backports must be checked with the distribution vendor.

python-certificates.title: Python releases address the known certificate incident
python-certificates.description: Python 3.15.1, 3.14.9 and 3.13.17 update bundled pip to 26.2.2, including certifi 2026.10.19, in response to the already reported eMudhra/emSign certificate incident. The release announcement also instructs users to update pip and uv in existing virtual environments. Knowing the interpreter version alone does not establish which pip and certificates an existing virtual environment uses.

python-alpha.title: Python 3.16 development preview
python-alpha.description: Python 3.16.0a1 is an early developer preview and the first planned alpha. The announcement invites library and application maintainers to test compatibility and report bugs. It warns against production use and describes the development schedule. This scenario contains no vulnerability report or security fix.

cases.system_context: DNS service validates untrusted hostnames and then invokes dns.resolve
cases.expected_reason: The target runtime precedes the fixed 26.x release and the supplied deployment uses the affected DNS path.
The installed version is explicitly listed as a security release fixing the target issue.
A Node.js organization keyword does not identify Corepack as the affected runtime. The scenario supplies no Corepack or underlying runtime applicability evidence.

cases.system_context: Internet-facing PHP-FPM using upstream PHP builds without distribution backports
cases.expected_reason: An upstream PHP-FPM release immediately before the fixed release meets the described deployment and version conditions.
The exact installed release is identified as fixing this target vulnerability.
The missing installed version prevents a decisive impact claim.

cases.system_context: Upstream PHP-FPM without backports; session upload progress disabled but no security update installed
cases.expected_reason: The stated mitigation blocks only some attack paths; it does not establish that the vulnerable installation is safe.
The production evidence gate must preserve uncertainty when the supplied article is marked incomplete, even if its excerpt mentions a fixed version.

cases.system_context: Existing virtual environment; pip and certificate bundle versions have not been inventoried
cases.expected_reason: This updates a known security incident; interpreter version alone does not establish the existing environment's certificate state.
The supplied developer-preview scenario contains no vulnerability claim to apply to this installation.
